To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a regularized training objective that can be used for continued training of NMT models for domain adaptation, and that it improves over standard continued training.

(1) the continued training objective is a regularized objective, (2) it is possible to improve the performance of continued training by adding an auxiliary term that minimizes the difference between the output distributions of the out-of- and in-domain models, (3) the auxiliary term can be added as a regularization term during continued training.
we have developed an auxiliary term for continued training in domain adaptation that improves the BLEU score by up to 0.8 points on the TED and 1.5 points on the EMEA datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the use of a regularized training objective to improve the quality of in-domain neural machine translation (2) the use of an auxiliary loss term to reduce the divergence of the output word distributions of the generic model and in-domain model (3) the use of the auxiliary loss term to prevent overfitting of the in-domain model to the in-domain data.
